local_checks.result: Re-checked at 8f393491 (U310b on e92b4970): the omp-gateway plugin and its tests are unchanged; the hcom-seat lines below are re-mapped to this head. DEFAULT_ENV_NAMES gains OMP_PROFILE and nothing else (config.mjs:10-13), with the reason beside it (:3-9). The plugin spawns the child with pickEnv(config.env) (index.mjs:73), and pickEnv copies only listed names that exist in the plugin's own environment (gateway-client.mjs:26-33), so OMP_PROFILE reaches the child only when the launcher set it; under hcom-seat's dsh role that value is the lever's own OMP_PROFILE=dsh, set under env -i (hcom-seat:2438). The list still names no credential: the use-case test asserts no KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, OAUTH or PASSWORD name (test/use-cases.test.mjs:622-626), and the new recorder test asserts the child carries OMP_PROFILE when the plugin has it and not when it is unset, with a non-row name dropped (test/gateway-client.test.mjs:251-283). The value moves the child from ~/.omp/agent, which the dsh role denies, to ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, which the role already grants for read and write (hcom-seat:1664, :1965) and which the judge pins to its own position (:1971-1975); srt still denies every other profile, so a different value would fail as the g6 run did, not widen. The row's `env` can replace the list (config.mjs:37), but the profile file is the operator's managed file, and a value only ever comes from the plugin's own environment. Outside hcom-seat, an operator running dsh directly forwards their own OMP_PROFILE to their own child.

hardening_notes: With OMP_PROFILE=dsh the gateway child keeps its omp state, agent.db and whatever login state omp stores there, in ~/.omp/profiles/dsh, a dsh write root the contained session can read and rewrite (hcom-seat:1664, :1965). The child's environment carries no token name, so its Claude login is read from that profile or from a source this run may not inspect. If it is a stored refresh credential, it is a second copy of the operator's login inside the sandbox beside the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN the shim exports (carried pattern), and it would outlive the launch. Not verified: the profile's contents are a credential store.

On a host whose stat messages are translated (GNU coreutils with a language pack, for example the ja locale the Ubuntu client profile installs language-pack-ja for), the second presence read after a good removal would print the translated ENOENT text and refuse, so every dsh launch there would end 2 naming a slot that is gone. Such a process still holds write access to the state slot and could race the operator's chmod -R and rm -rf traversal, for example by swapping a directory for a link mid-walk. Renaming the slot out of the write root first (into the write-denied .sandbox, say) and removing it there would close that window.
